Sanjay K: Heads up — seeing steady mem growth on kv-cache hosts when continuous-batching is enabled. Starts small then drifts over ~12h on long-context workloads.
Ruth Cheng: Ugh. Is this the paging/eviction path or actual fragmentation?
Sanjay K: Initial heap dumps look like lots of tiny free slabs; allocator not reusing adjacent slots — fragmentation. But evictions are rare, even under pressure.
Tom R: Could be because we merge heterogeneous batches and then split heads, leaving orphaned kv slices. Do you have a repro?
Sanjay K: Minimal repro attached (long-ctx chat sim, 64 concurrent streams). I can run with extra tracing but wanted to surface first.
Claire Li: @Sanjay K can you post the batch merge logs and the kv index snapshot? Also include kernel selection — we saw different GEMM kernels change cache layout before.
Sanjay K: Paste logs below:
```
[batch] merge 100->27 groups, avg len 1024
[kv] alloc shard 5 size 65536 token_entries=800
[kv] reuse miss: candidate_fragments=12
[kv] pageout triggered: scanned 4 slabs, reclaimed 0
[kv] eviction: policy=LRU age_threshold=3600 reclaimed=2
```
Ruth Cheng: Interesting that pageout reclaimed 0 slabs. That suggests holes too small to coalesce. Any ongoing compaction?
Sanjay K: Compaction runs async but we throttle it when CPU > 70%. On these runs CPU stays ~50% so shouldn't be throttled.
Tom R: Could continuous-batching merge create many small KV writes for prefills (kv put ranges) that split existing slabs? If split pattern is worst-case it fragments.
Claire Li: Also check head-of-line blocking: if one large request holds a KV shard lock, small requests queue and create many small allocations on different threads. Leads to interleaved fragmentation.
Sanjay K: I observed lots of batch split ops: `split_at=900` then `emit_batch(100)` repeatedly. Might be from max-token heuristics sending head out.
perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: /perf/traces/1736204129/kvfrag-merge-01.trace
Ruth Cheng: Can you run with `KV_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=16` and `BATCH_MERGE_SIZE=512` to force coarser merges and more aggressive compaction? Should be low-risk on prod.
Sanjay K: Running now on a canary pool with those env flags. Also toggling `ALLOW_KERNEL_FALLBACK=0` to keep the same kernel so we remove kernel-switch as a confounder.
Tom R: If that reduces growth, we know merge granularity + compaction tuning is the culprit. If not, we should profile allocator activity with dmalloc hooks to see split pattern.
Claire Li: Also add `kv.debug.reuse_hist=1` to logs — want to see reuse window distribution.
Sanjay K: Can everyone check the perf trace link and I'll post before/after heapdiffs in ~30m.
Ruth Cheng: +1. If we confirm fragmentation, we can add an opportunistic coalesce pass during low-qps windows or change merge policy to prefer homogeneous sequence lengths.
Tom R: Also consider adding a per-shard freelist compaction when free_count exceeds threshold to avoid long-term leakage.
Sanjay K: Canary running. Early signs: allocation churn down ~30% after BATCH_MERGE_SIZE=512. Heap growth slope reduced but not gone. Will post numbers.
Claire Li: Sweet. If that holds, we should roll to more clusters with a gradual ramp and monitor tail latency — merging bigger can affect latency for short requests.
Sanjay K: Agreed. Will include tail p95/p99 in next post. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
